text:
maria: FYI finance asked for a Q2 breakdown of spot savings vs on-demand for the GPU fleet. They want: realized savings, variance, and a reconciliation to billed dollars for chargeback. Can we get a strawman by EOD?
aj: I can pull the raw instance-hour data and interruption logs. do they want per-region / per-instance-type?
ryan: Per-region and per-pool please. The chargeback team needs to map back to customer-facing business units so granularness matters. Also include the cost of interruptions (retries, wasted minutes).
katie: Quick note: our billing exports show gross spot spend and gross on-demand spend, but not the interruption overhead. We should calculate effective consumed hours = allocated hours - wasted_preempt_hours.
maria: Right — suggested deliverables: 1) point estimates of average discount (spot vs on-demand) per instance family/region, 2) volatility (std dev, 95th pct) of hourly savings, 3) estimated interruption cost adjustment, 4) reconciliation table to the billed amounts for chargeback.
aj: plan: run two queries: A) hourly instance-state join for Q2 to get hours and interruptions per instance_id B) price lookup to compute on-demand vs spot price per hour. I have a helper SQL that outputs: (region, instance_type, pool, date, spot_hours, on_demand_hours, interruptions, wasted_hours).
aj: snippet: ```-- simplified
SELECT region, machine, SUM(spot_hours) AS spot_h, SUM(interruptions) AS interrupts
FROM gpu_instance_hours
WHERE ts BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2025-06-30'
GROUP BY region, machine
```
ryan: For interruption cost model, use: interruption_cost = wasted_hours * on_demand_rate + retry_overhead_hours * on_demand_rate. Where retry_overhead_hours = median_restart_time * number_of_preempted_jobs / 3600. Use 95th pct as a sensitivity case.
katie: Also include a model for checkpoint-enabled jobs vs ephemeral jobs. Ephemeral <-> full restart penalty is much higher. We have checkpoint fraction per pool available in metrics: checkpoint_rate. Multiply wasted_hours by (1 - checkpoint_rate)*full_restart_penalty_factor.
maria: Good. We should pick baseline assumptions and then a +/- sensitivity: baseline = median restart 8m, full_restart_penalty_factor = 1.2 (extra IO and queued time), conservative = 15m & 1.5, optimistic = 4m & 1.0.
ryan: Finance asked how to represent savings variance in the chargeback. Two options: A) show realized savings as-is and leave volatility visible, B) use smoothing (30d rolling average) for chargebacks to avoid big monthly swings. They prefer B for predictability.
aj: Implementation detail: chargeback pipeline currently uses daily aggregates. If we do 30d smoothing, we can compute rolling_spot_unit_cost = rolling(sum_paid_spot_hours_cost)/rolling(sum_spot_hours_served). Then allocate per BU by their effective hours.
katie: Important: on-demand spot-equivalent price lookup: we must lock the on-demand price to the published on-demand hourly at the time the instance ran. AWS/GCP on-demand prices changed for some families mid-Q2 in eu-west. Use price_history table.
maria: Anything else? network egress cost differences between regions? That can skew unit economics for multi-region jobs. Finance only asked for GPU costs first, but call out egress as note.
ryan: I'll need the raw numbers to reconcile to payments in the ledger. Please include an "adjustment" line for interruptions and one for reserved/dedicated discounts (we bill certain workloads to dedicated pools differently).
aj: I can produce a CSV with columns: region,machine,pool,spot_hours,spot_paid,$spot_paid,on_demand_cost,$on_demand_cost,savings_pct,interrupts,wasted_hours,adj_cost. Then a summary sheet with per-BU allocated costs under both raw and smoothed methods.
ops-bot: deploy:chargeback-pipeline reported success for DailyAggregateJob at 2025-06-30T02:12:11Z :white_check_mark:
maria: Timeline: aj will produce the raw CSV + summary by EOD. I (maria) and ryan will validate and create the reconciliation sheet for finance tomorrow. Katie will annotate checkpoints and special-case pools.
aj: quick numbers preview (VERY ROUGH): across Q2 aggregate spot discount = ~62% (weighted), std dev of hourly savings ~12 percentage points, 95th pct savings day ~78%, worst day ~35% (lots of preemptions). Interruption overhead estimated ~3.5% of on-demand equivalent spend baseline.
katie: That aligns with our metrics — eu-west had higher interruption variance. Also note mixed pools with small on-demand fallback show much lower variance but lower absolute discount (~45%).
ryan: For finance memo, I'll recommend presenting: realized savings, smoothed chargeback numbers (30d), plus an appendix with volatility metrics and interruption adjustment methodology. Also request a reconciliation CSV that maps to ledger invoice ids.
maria: Thanks team. If anyone sees a discrepancy between the chargeback CSV and ledger, flag it here and we'll schedule a 15m sync. :calendar: :money_with_wings: 
aj: uploading CSV to gs://redwood-internal/chargeback/q2_spot_recon.csv now. link: https://storage.redwood/g/q2_spot_recon.csv
ryan: Got it. I'll start recon and share a draft memo by tomorrow morning.
katie: I'll add checkpoint fractions to the CSV as an extra column.
maria: Closing the thread once the memo is attached. Great work. :thumbsup:
